evidence.V1: Front outline is a symmetric crown + pointed pavilion (A15 X/Y error 0.0), the three-quarter silhouette still reads as a cut gem, and the top view reads as an octagonal cushion; recognisable at 64 px from every angle.
evidence.V2: Clear tiers: big = crown vs pavilion mass; medium = table, ring of bezel facets, girdle band, pavilion main facets; small = corner facets and chamfer lines. The pavilion is the plainest part but its facet breaks still read.
evidence.V3: Chunky stylised proportion: a shallow crown about 1/3 of the height over a deep pointed pavilion, with a slightly elongated top (0.95 x 0.80 studs); reads as a confident stylised gem, not a stiff primitive.
evidence.V4: Thin chamfers run consistently along the table rim, the bezel edges and the girdle, and catch light as bright lines in the studio close-ups, matching the kit's soft-edge look.
evidence.V5: Minor: some planar facets shade unevenly under Workbench studio light, so smoothed normals bleed across faces that should be flat. There is a soft wide highlight smear at the bezel/table corner in the crown close-up, a horizontal light streak across the crown in the front view, and top-to-bottom gradients on the left crown and pavilion facets. No seams, pinches or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: One hue in three values (light table, mid crown, dark pavilion) with strong value contrast; the crimson and royal colourways keep the same value structure.
evidence.V7: 286 tris against the small-class target of 600 (ceiling 1500), so well under target.
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material with vertex colours, a single kit hue in up to 3 values, chamfered edges and smooth shading; matches the kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line is correct for a pickup: CanCollide off, CanTouch on, Box fidelity, Anchored, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin at centre.

artifacts: Smoothed normals bleed across planar facets: soft highlight smear at the bezel/table corner (crown studio close-up) and gradient shading inside crown and pavilion facets that should shade flat
top_fixes: Make each planar facet shade flat: split normals at every facet edge (sharp edges / weighted normals with face-strength) so the chamfers carry the highlight and the facets themselves stay uniform
Add a bit more definition to the pavilion (one clear lighter value step or a visible keel line on the main facets) so the lower half doesn't read as one dark mass at small sizes
